title: DAC 2026: How Undo Makes AI for Chip Design Work Better - Semiwiki
gist: A DAC 2026 vendor profile of Undo, whose deterministic record-and-replay technology captures a program's exact execution history so AI coding agents can do evidence-based root-cause analysis on C/C++ and SystemC codebases up to 100x faster. The core argument is that model intelligence is no longer the bottleneck in agentic chip design - runtime context is - and that debug consumes roughly 35% of total silicon design effort.

themes.theme: Context, not model quality, is the AI bottleneck

insights.claim: The limiting factor for AI coding agents on complex codebases is missing runtime context, not model intelligence - execution paths, state changes and cross-module values that source code and logs never reveal.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Reframes where value accrues in agentic engineering tooling: toward context-capture infrastructure rather than toward foundation models.
insights.quote: This isn't a gap in the model's intelligence; it's a gap in its context.
insights.locator: Coding agents get stuck in the same human loop

insights.claim: Logs are structurally insufficient as AI context because they only capture what was predicted in advance to be interesting - if you already knew which data would expose the bug, you would have prevented it.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: A clean argument for why observability-by-instrumentation loses to full-execution recording, and why log-analysis AI tools have a ceiling.
insights.quote: logs only show what was predicted to be of interest. If you already knew which data would expose the problem, you'd have prevented it in the first place.
insights.locator: The problem is you can't truly see what happened at runtime

insights.claim: Agents without runtime recording fall into the same re-instrument-and-rerun loop humans use, executing it faster but with equally wasted cycles.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Explains why headline agent speedups fail to translate into throughput on hard debug work - a caution on productivity claims from agent vendors.
insights.quote: Coding agents get stuck in the same human loop of re-instrumenting and rerunning. This is done faster, but it is just as wasteful.
insights.locator: Coding agents get stuck in the same human loop

insights.claim: Runtime context from the live design is asserted to be more valuable than static training data or generic LLM intelligence for verification root-cause analysis.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: If true, proprietary runtime data - not model access - is the defensible asset in EDA AI, favoring incumbents who own the execution environment.
insights.quote: Runtime context from the live design is far more valuable than static training data or generic LLM intelligence.
insights.locator: System verification teams can reduce debug time

insights.claim: Undo's deterministic technology records a program's exact execution once - every variable, event and I/O across every module - and agents then query that recording rather than re-running the program.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Record-once-query-many is the architectural claim; it converts debug from repeated compute into a data-query problem, which is what makes it agent-compatible.
insights.quote: Undo's deterministic technology records a program's exact execution once: every variable, every event, every I/O, across every module.
insights.locator: He went on to explain that Undo's deterministic technology

insights.claim: Undo claims high-quality runtime context enables evidence-based automated root-cause analysis up to 100x faster, focused on C/C++ and SystemC.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: The 100x figure is the vendor's headline ROI claim; C/C++ and SystemC scoping shows the beachhead is simulation models and firmware, not RTL.
insights.quote: Undo enables evidence-based automated root-cause analysis up to 100x faster
insights.locator: Greg explained that Undo enables AI to understand

insights.claim: With execution recordings, rare, intermittent and complex bugs - the class that resists reproduction - become tractable to isolate and explain.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Non-reproducible bugs are the highest-cost category in silicon bring-up; addressing them is where willingness-to-pay concentrates.
insights.quote: rare, intermittent and complex problems become easy to isolate and explain
insights.locator: Agents then query the recording to reason about dynamic behavior

insights.claim: The stated effect of runtime context is to convert an AI agent from a clever guesser into a reliable problem-solver that can explain why a failure occurred, not just what failed.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Explainability backed by a recording is the trust mechanism that lets agentic debug clear sign-off gates in regulated or high-cost design flows.
insights.quote: It transforms an agent from a “clever guesser” into a reliable problem-solver.
insights.locator: Looking closer, for AI this context is quite valuable

themes.theme: Debug is 35% of silicon design effort

insights.claim: Citing Wilson Research Group, up to 70% of design investment goes into verification and roughly 50% of that time into debug - implying about 35% of total silicon design effort is spent on debug alone.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Sizes the TAM for debug automation at roughly a third of all design labor - the strongest quantitative case for EDA AI spend.
insights.quote: up to 70% of design investment goes into verification. And roughly 50% of that time goes into debug.

insights.claim: System-level bugs can originate in the test bench, fast models, synthetic software load, or RTL - or in the interactions between them - which is why single-domain debug tools fail at root-cause analysis.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Cross-domain bug localization is the unmet need; tools confined to one abstraction layer are structurally disadvantaged.
insights.quote: bugs can be anywhere (the test bench, fast models, the synthetic software load, or RTL hardware design)
insights.locator: Root cause analysis is challenging since bugs can be anywhere

insights.claim: Large SystemC and C++ simulation models are opaque and multi-threaded, making them especially hard and time-consuming to debug relative to other verification artifacts.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Multi-threaded opacity is exactly what deterministic replay solves, explaining why Undo targets this niche first.
insights.quote: large SystemC and C++ simulation models are often opaque and multi-threaded, making them especially hard and time-consuming to debug
insights.locator: Bugs can be in any of these domains

themes.theme: GPU architecture exploration constrained by coverage

insights.claim: System architects running test workloads on GPU models reach only 50-60% coverage of meaningful use cases because functional bugs block enough applications from running on the model, directly degrading final chip quality.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: A concrete number on how much architectural design space goes unexplored - upside for any tool that lifts coverage translates into better silicon, not just faster schedules.
insights.quote: coverage may only reach 50 – 60% of meaningful use cases. The inability to perform more tests impacts the final quality of the chip.

insights.claim: Undo positions its recordings as data unobtainable by any other method, making the claim a data-moat argument rather than an algorithmic one.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Test the exclusivity claim against emulation and hardware-trace alternatives - it is the load-bearing assumption in the investment case.
insights.quote: Undo provides the needed runtime context – and you can't get that data any other way.

insights.claim: DAC 2026 was dominated by AI-fueled chip design and debug tools promising higher quality designs faster with fewer resources, with the emerging counterweight being AI losing focus and context on very complex designs.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: The industry narrative has moved from can-AI-design-chips to can-AI-stay-grounded, which is where the next EDA tooling spend goes.
insights.quote: For AI-driven chip design some of those risks center around a class of issues associated with AI losing its focus and context.

insights.claim: Engineering teams adopting Cursor, Claude and Copilot are actively questioning whether these agents scale to large complex codebases and how much hallucination limits the benefit.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Named-tool adoption is broad but confidence is not - the gap is the market opening for grounding/context layers sold alongside agents.
insights.quote: These teams often question whether they can scale to large and complex codebases. There is a concern about how much hallucination (returning results not grounded in fact) limits the benefits.
insights.locator: Stepping back a bit, we can look at coding agents
